findings.issue: The 30-word lead ('Since 2011 we have run bulk lines…') and the aqua CONTACT US pill are still on the photo, centred in four lines under the title, though the site rule puts a lead much longer than the competitor's under the hero.
findings.reference: The competitor's About hero is the factory photo with only the centred white H1 on it: no lead and no button.
findings.fix: Set the on-photo lead limit per page type (heroText.leadWords; the about reference has 0 words), so PageHero.astro's heroLeadShown() moves the about lead and its button into the block under the hero.

findings.issue: On phones the same lead still runs to four lines of small centred text over the busy rose-and-wall photo, between the three-line title and the large aqua pill, so the lower half of the hero is all text over the picture.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone hero carries only the white H1 over the photo; its text comes after the photo.
findings.fix: Use the same per-page-type lead limit in PageHero.astro (heroLeadShown()), so the about lead and its button go under the hero at every width.

findings.issue: On /about-us/ the 'About Us' nav item still looks like the other items: no component in src/ sets aria-current on a nav link (only Breadcrumbs and pagination do), so the treatment's `.site-nav__link[aria-current="page"]` rule (lighter #d3ebfd, underline) never applies.
findings.reference: The competitor's header shows the current page's item ('About') in a lighter tone.
findings.fix: In SiteHeader.astro, set aria-current="page" on the nav link (and dropdown sublink) whose route matches the current page.

findings.issue: Two of the four figures still read as cut-off phrases ('65 that' over 'SAMPLING TEAM', '55 custom' over 'DAILY SAMPLES'). On phones '100,000 pieces' wraps to two lines, so 'MONTHLY CAPACITY' sits lower than 'FOUNDED' beside it.
findings.reference: The competitor's figure rows set a short value over a clear uppercase label.
findings.fix: Site Factory: rewrite the value/label pairs, e.g. '65' / 'person sampling team', '55' / 'custom samples a day', '100,000' / 'pieces a month'.

findings.issue: The six steps wrap into two rows of three, but the connecting line still runs only through the first row and on past marker 03 to the column edge, while steps 04–06 have no line, so the second row looks detached from the sequence.
findings.reference: The competitor's step module sets every step on the same hairline.
findings.fix: Draw the process rule per row, on each row's marker line instead of one line across the whole step list, and end it at the row's last marker.

findings.issue: After m6's tint, the logo row, the testimonials and the FAQ still stand on white one after another (the same at 390px), while every section above them alternates.
findings.reference: The site rule: neighbouring plain sections alternate white and tinted backgrounds, set by the template.
findings.fix: Make the template's section-surface alternation count the logos and testimonials blocks, so the testimonials section takes --section-tint and breaks up the white run.

findings.issue: m5 ('How We Check Quality at Every Stage') and m6 ('Certifications and Compliance Paperwork') are still both a heading with a check list of short items beside it, one under the other, so only the background changes between them.
findings.reference: The site rule: two sections of the same shape do not stand one under the other; the template sets only one of them out as a list beside its heading.
findings.fix: In the template's layout pass, when two adjacent iconList sections both have the list-beside-heading shape, set the second one out differently (e.g. a two-column check grid under its heading).

findings.issue: The tall phone frame still crops the photo to its stone wall and roses, with only part of the sitter's dress at the lower-right edge, so the subject is almost out of the frame.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone hero uses its own phone crop (banner-about-us-mobile.webp), so the scene stays in the frame.
findings.fix: Give the about hero photo a phone crop or a focal point on the sitter, set by the template (--hero-focal or a phone image source), not by reference.css.

findings.issue: The second question breaks at the hyphen of 'in-house' ('…pattern makers in-' / 'house to develop our styles?'), so the heading reads as a hyphenated word split across two lines.
findings.reference: The competitor's headings keep their words whole on one line.
findings.fix: Site Factory: write 'in‑house' with a non-breaking hyphen (U+2011) in the FAQ question (or reword it as 'in your own studio'), so the compound stays on one line.

findings.issue: On phones, where the carousel shows one quote card at a time, the card has a blank strip about 70px tall between the five-line quote and its rule. This is because the subgrid levelling added in reference.css sizes the quote track to the hidden second card's longer quote.
findings.reference: The competitor's quote cards close their attribution under the quote with no empty band.
findings.fix: In reference.css, apply the `.testimonials[data-variant="carousel"]:not(:has(.testimonial__headline))` subgrid rules only when cards share a row (inside @media (min-width: 768px) or under `.track[data-fits]`), so a single phone card sizes to its own quote.
